# Related Work References — event-gated-adaptive-horizon
# Generated: 2026-05-16
# Total: 25 papers across 5 categories (≥4 per category)
# Purpose: CoRL 2026 Related Work section expansion

# ============================================================
# Category 1: Temporal Abstraction in MBRL (6 papers)
# ============================================================

- key: hafner2023dreamerv3
  title: "Mastering Diverse Domains through World Models"
  authors: "Hafner et al."
  venue: "arXiv 2023 / Nature 2025"
  year: 2023
  category: "Temporal Abstraction in MBRL"
  relevance: "Base system we modify; RSSM + symlog + imagination-based actor-critic training with fixed horizon."

- key: hansen2022tdmpc
  title: "Temporal Difference Learning for Model Predictive Control"
  authors: "Hansen et al."
  venue: "ICML 2022"
  year: 2022
  category: "Temporal Abstraction in MBRL"
  relevance: "Combines learned latent dynamics with TD-learning for MPC; shows how TD targets shape effective planning horizon in model-based control."

- key: hansen2024tdmpc2
  title: "TD-MPC2: Scalable, Robust World Models for Continuous Control"
  authors: "Hansen et al."
  venue: "ICLR 2024"
  year: 2024
  category: "Temporal Abstraction in MBRL"
  relevance: "Scales latent-space MPC planning across 104 tasks; uses online planning (not imagination-based training), contrasting with DreamerV3 paradigm."

- key: hafner2022director
  title: "Deep Hierarchical Planning from Pixels"
  authors: "Hafner et al."
  venue: "NeurIPS 2022"
  year: 2022
  category: "Temporal Abstraction in MBRL"
  relevance: "Hierarchical goal-conditioned planning in Dreamer latent space; addresses temporal abstraction via goal hierarchy rather than variable dt."

- key: gumbsch2024thick
  title: "Learning Hierarchical World Models with Adaptive Temporal Abstractions from Discrete Latent Dynamics"
  authors: "Gumbsch et al."
  venue: "ICLR 2024"
  year: 2024
  category: "Temporal Abstraction in MBRL"
  relevance: "THICK — learns adaptive temporal abstractions via context-change detection in Dreamer; closest concurrent work addressing temporal abstraction via hierarchy."

- key: nhu2025tawm
  title: "Time-Aware World Model for Adaptive Prediction and Control"
  authors: "Nhu et al."
  venue: "ICML 2025"
  year: 2025
  category: "Temporal Abstraction in MBRL"
  relevance: "TAWM — explicitly conditions world model on Δt for multi-rate dynamics; built on TD-MPC2 (MPC, not imagination). Treats Δt conditioning as beneficial — opposite to our finding that it causes CIVO in imagination-based training."

# ============================================================
# Category 2: Value Overestimation / Collapse (5 papers)
# ============================================================

- key: fujimoto2018td3
  title: "Addressing Function Approximation Error in Actor-Critic Methods"
  authors: "Fujimoto et al."
  venue: "ICML 2018"
  year: 2018
  category: "Value Overestimation / Collapse"
  relevance: "TD3 — canonical reference for overestimation bias in actor-critic; clipped double-Q mitigation. DreamerV3 uses single critic, making it more vulnerable."

- key: chen2021redq
  title: "Randomized Ensembled Double Q-Learning: Learning Fast Without a Model"
  authors: "Chen et al."
  venue: "ICLR 2021"
  year: 2021
  category: "Value Overestimation / Collapse"
  relevance: "REDQ — ensemble Q-functions with in-target minimization to control overestimation at high UTD ratios; shows model-free can match MBRL when overestimation is controlled."

- key: lyle2023plasticity
  title: "Understanding Plasticity in Neural Networks"
  authors: "Lyle et al."
  venue: "ICML 2023"
  year: 2023
  category: "Value Overestimation / Collapse"
  relevance: "Shows deep RL networks progressively lose plasticity due to curvature changes; compounds value estimation errors and can precipitate policy collapse."

- key: sokar2023dormant
  title: "The Dormant Neuron Phenomenon in Deep Reinforcement Learning"
  authors: "Sokar et al."
  venue: "ICML 2023"
  year: 2023
  category: "Value Overestimation / Collapse"
  relevance: "Identifies dormant neurons reducing network expressivity during RL training; directly impairs critic capacity and contributes to value collapse."

- key: tang2024chain
  title: "Improving Deep Reinforcement Learning by Reducing the Chain Effect of Value and Policy Churn"
  authors: "Tang & Berseth"
  venue: "NeurIPS 2024"
  year: 2024
  category: "Value Overestimation / Collapse"
  relevance: "Characterizes chain effect where value churn and policy churn compound across iterations; synthetic rollouts in MBRL amplify this churn."

# ============================================================
# Category 3: Gradient Interference / Stop-gradient (5 papers)
# ============================================================

- key: ma2024harmonydream
  title: "HarmonyDream: Task Harmonization Inside World Models"
  authors: "Ma et al."
  venue: "ICML 2024"
  year: 2024
  category: "Gradient Interference / Stop-gradient"
  relevance: "Shows observation prediction dominates reward prediction in world model training; proposes dynamic loss balancing — most directly comparable to our SGS gradient blocking."

- key: jaderberg2017unreal
  title: "Reinforcement Learning with Unsupervised Auxiliary Tasks"
  authors: "Jaderberg et al."
  venue: "ICLR 2017"
  year: 2017
  category: "Gradient Interference / Stop-gradient"
  relevance: "UNREAL — reward prediction as auxiliary task shapes shared representations; foundational evidence that auxiliary losses actively condition feature learning."

- key: lyle2021auxiliary
  title: "On The Effect of Auxiliary Tasks on Representation Dynamics"
  authors: "Lyle et al."
  venue: "AISTATS 2021"
  year: 2021
  category: "Gradient Interference / Stop-gradient"
  relevance: "Theoretical analysis showing auxiliary tasks shape representations toward top eigenvectors of transition operator; explains how removing temporal conditioning alters representation structure."

- key: li2022ssl_rl
  title: "Does Self-Supervised Learning Really Improve Reinforcement Learning from Pixels?"
  authors: "Li et al."
  venue: "NeurIPS 2022"
  year: 2022
  category: "Gradient Interference / Stop-gradient"
  relevance: "Shows no single SSL auxiliary loss universally helps pixel-based RL; joint optimization of SSL and RL objectives has fundamental limitations — evidence decoder losses can interfere with policy-relevant representations."

- key: sun2024hrssm
  title: "Learning Latent Dynamic Robust Representations for World Models"
  authors: "Sun et al."
  venue: "ICML 2024"
  year: 2024
  category: "Gradient Interference / Stop-gradient"
  relevance: "HRSSM — applies spatio-temporal masking to filter task-irrelevant details from reconstruction targets; directly tackles observation decoder gradients corrupting temporal embeddings."

# ============================================================
# Category 4: World Model Diagnostics (5 papers)
# ============================================================

- key: janner2019mbpo
  title: "When to Trust Your Model: Model-Based Policy Optimization"
  authors: "Janner et al."
  venue: "NeurIPS 2019"
  year: 2019
  category: "World Model Diagnostics"
  relevance: "MBPO — derives monotonic improvement bounds linking model error and rollout horizon to policy degradation; motivates adaptive horizon approaches."

- key: lambert2020objective
  title: "Objective Mismatch in Model-based Reinforcement Learning"
  authors: "Lambert et al."
  venue: "L4DC 2020"
  year: 2020
  category: "World Model Diagnostics"
  relevance: "Shows one-step prediction accuracy does not correlate with control performance; our work reveals a specific instance where reward MAE directly gates value stability."

- key: hamrick2021planning
  title: "On the Role of Planning in Model-Based Deep Reinforcement Learning"
  authors: "Hamrick et al."
  venue: "ICLR 2021"
  year: 2021
  category: "World Model Diagnostics"
  relevance: "Systematic MuZero ablation showing planning's primary value is in learning (not test-time); shallow rollouts suffice — supports our finding that dt=1 imagination is sufficient."

- key: talvitie2017selfcorrecting
  title: "Self-Correcting Models for Model-Based Reinforcement Learning"
  authors: "Talvitie"
  venue: "AAAI 2017"
  year: 2017
  category: "World Model Diagnostics"
  relevance: "Introduces hallucinated replay to analyze multi-step error compounding; proves self-correction ability (not one-step accuracy) predicts MBRL performance."

- key: vafa2024evaluating
  title: "Evaluating the World Model Implicit in a Generative Model"
  authors: "Vafa et al."
  venue: "NeurIPS 2024 (Spotlight)"
  year: 2024
  category: "World Model Diagnostics"
  relevance: "Formalizes world model evaluation via Myhill-Nerode theory; reveals models appearing accurate on standard metrics can harbor incoherent internal representations."

# ============================================================
# Category 5: Selective Gradient / SGS techniques (4 papers)
# ============================================================

- key: yu2020pcgrad
  title: "Gradient Surgery for Multi-Task Learning"
  authors: "Yu et al."
  venue: "NeurIPS 2020"
  year: 2020
  category: "Selective Gradient / SGS techniques"
  relevance: "PCGrad — projects conflicting task gradients onto each other's normal planes; foundational gradient surgery method directly analogous to our SGS selective gradient blocking."

- key: liu2021cagrad
  title: "Conflict-Averse Gradient Descent for Multi-task Learning"
  authors: "Liu et al."
  venue: "NeurIPS 2021"
  year: 2021
  category: "Selective Gradient / SGS techniques"
  relevance: "CAGrad — finds common descent direction avoiding worst-case task conflict with convergence guarantees; optimization-based alternative to SGS's event-gated blocking."

- key: wang2021gradientvaccine
  title: "Gradient Vaccine: Investigating and Improving Multi-task Optimization in Massively Multilingual Models"
  authors: "Wang et al."
  venue: "ICLR 2021"
  year: 2021
  category: "Selective Gradient / SGS techniques"
  relevance: "Uses gradient similarity to detect and mitigate task conflicts in shared representations; parallels SGS's use of event signals to decide when gradient flow should be blocked."

- key: navon2022nashmtl
  title: "Multi-Task Learning as a Bargaining Game"
  authors: "Navon et al."
  venue: "ICML 2022"
  year: 2022
  category: "Selective Gradient / SGS techniques"
  relevance: "Nash-MTL — game-theoretic gradient combination ensuring proportional fairness among tasks; offers bargaining perspective on the inter-task interference SGS addresses."

# 1. STOCHASTIC COLLAPSE HAS PRECEDENT:
#    Plasticity loss (Lyle 2022, Sokar 2023, Nikishin 2023) is inherently
#    seed-dependent because it depends on initialization → early gradient
#    dynamics → neuron activity patterns. Different seeds hit different
#    plasticity trajectories under identical configs.
#
# 2. nve>1.5x AS DIAGNOSTIC MARKER (necessary but not sufficient):
#    Lyle 2022 shows feature rank collapse is necessary but not sufficient
#    for learning failure. Kumar 2022 shows feature aliasing from TD
#    learning creates the overestimation substrate. Our nve>1.5x is
#    analogous: it indicates the dt_embedding has enabled value exploitation
#    (100% reliable marker), but collapse requires additional conditions
#    (plasticity loss, insufficient effective LR decay) that are stochastic.
#
# 3. SELF-CORRECTION MECHANISM:
#    Lyle 2024 provides a candidate mechanism: normalization-induced
#    effective LR decay can naturally damp overestimation in some seeds.
#    Farebrother 2024 shows categorical value training provides partial
#    implicit regularization. Together these explain why seed 2 self-corrects:
#    the combination of DreamerV3's categorical critic + normalization +
#    favorable initialization produces enough implicit regularization to
#    overcome the dt_embedding-induced overestimation.
#
# 4. THEORETICAL GROUNDING:
#    Zhang 2026 (already in map) provides the dynamical systems framework.
#    Bjorck 2022 (already in map) shows early outlier events dominate
#    variance. Together with the new papers, the framing is:
#    "trained dt_embedding creates a necessary condition (nve>1.5x) for
#    CIVO collapse, but collapse is a stochastic bifurcation
#    whose outcome depends on seed-dependent plasticity dynamics."

# world model on Δt — closest methodological overlap. But TAWM
# uses TD-MPC2 (online MPC) not imagination-based actor-critic,

- paper_id: nhu2025tawm
  title: "Time-Aware World Model for Adaptive Prediction and Control"
  authors: [Nhu A.N., Son S., Lin M.C.]
  year: 2025
  venue: "ICML 2025 (arXiv:2506.08441)"
  category: direct-competitor
  role: "TAWM — explicitly conditions world model on time-step size Δt and trains over diverse Δt values for multi-rate dynamics learning. Built on TD-MPC2 (online MPC). KEY DISTINCTION from our work: (1) TAWM treats Δt conditioning as beneficial for performance/data-efficiency; we diagnose it as pathological in imagination-based actor-critic training (CIVO). (2) TAWM uses MPC (no imagination rollouts for policy training); our failure mode is specific to imagination-based training where the critic exploits dt-conditioned value estimates. (3) TAWM focuses on observation-rate robustness; we focus on value overestimation from temporal conditioning corruption. TAWM actually strengthens our contribution: it shows Δt conditioning works in MPC settings, making our finding that it fails in imagination-based settings a surprising and important diagnostic."
  relevance_score: 5
  novelty_threat: "MEDIUM — methodological overlap (Δt conditioning) but fundamentally different paradigm (MPC vs imagination) and opposite conclusion (beneficial vs pathological). Must cite and differentiate in paper."

  authors: [Li J., Wang Q., Wang Y., Jin X., Li Y., Zeng W., Yang X.]
  year: 2025
  venue: "ICLR 2025 Oral (arXiv:2410.03618)"
  category: direct-competitor
  role: "LS-Imagine — extends imagination horizon in Dreamer via goal-conditioned jumpy state transitions and affordance maps. Addresses the 'short-sightedness' of standard Dreamer imagination. KEY DISTINCTION: LS-Imagine adds jumpy transitions to reach long-horizon targets (open-world Minecraft), while our work shows that variable-dt imagination itself introduces CIVO. LS-Imagine's jumpy transitions use goal conditioning (not dt-embedding), potentially avoiding the value overestimation we identify."
  relevance_score: 4
  novelty_threat: "LOW — different mechanism (goal-conditioned jumps vs dt-embedding) and different focus (long-horizon exploration vs diagnostic of failure modes). Should cite as concurrent approach to extending imagination horizon."

  venue: "arXiv:2604.03208"
  category: direct-competitor
  role: "HWM — learns multi-scale latent world models for hierarchical MPC planning; high-level planner optimizes macro-actions, low-level planner handles primitives. 70% success on real-world non-greedy robotic tasks vs 0% for single-level. Further evidence that temporal abstraction in world models requires hierarchy rather than single-scale variable-dt approaches."
  relevance_score: 4
  novelty_threat: "LOW — MPC-based hierarchical planning, not imagination-based training. Supports our thesis that flat dt-embedding approaches are inferior to hierarchical alternatives."

  venue: "NeurIPS 2023 (arXiv:2310.18534)"

  venue: "ICLR 2023 (arXiv:2204.09560)"
  category: background
  role: "Shows feature rank collapse from non-stationary TD targets is a necessary condition for learning failure but not sufficient — sparse rewards and other factors must co-occur.   year: 2022
  venue: "ICLR 2022"
  category: background
  role: "Shows implicit regularization from TD learning favors degenerate feature aliasing (states on both sides of Bellman backup become indistinguishable), creating the substrate for value overestimation. In our setting, trained dt_embedding amplifies this aliasing across different temporal horizons — the critic cannot distinguish between dt=1 and dt>1 value targets, enabling exploitation. Feature aliasing is seed-dependent because it depends on initialization geometry"

# Summary (2026-05-14):
#
# 1. STOCHASTIC COLLAPSE HAS PRECEDENT:
#    Plasticity loss (Lyle 2022, Sokar 2023, Nikishin 2023) is inherently
#    seed-dependent because it depends on initialization → early gradient
#    dynamics → neuron activity patterns. Different seeds hit different
#    plasticity trajectories under identical configs.
#
# 2. nve>1.5x AS DIAGNOSTIC MARKER (necessary but not sufficient):
#    Lyle 2022 shows feature rank collapse is necessary but not sufficient
#    for learning failure. Kumar 2022 shows feature aliasing from TD
#    learning creates the overestimation substrate. Our nve>1.5x is
#    analogous: it indicates the dt_embedding has enabled value exploitation
#    (100% reliable marker), but collapse requires additional conditions
#    (plasticity loss, insufficient effective LR decay) that are stochastic.
#
# 3. SELF-CORRECTION MECHANISM:
#    Lyle 2024 provides a candidate mechanism: normalization-induced
#    effective LR decay can naturally damp overestimation in some seeds.
#    Farebrother 2024 shows categorical value training provides partial
#    implicit regularization. Together these explain why seed 2 self-corrects:
#    the combination of DreamerV3's categorical critic + normalization +
#    favorable initialization produces enough implicit regularization to

#    whose outcome depends on seed-dependent plasticity dynamics."

# world model on Δt — closest methodological overlap. But TAWM

- paper_id: nhu2025tawm
  title: "Time-Aware World Model for Adaptive Prediction and Control"
  authors: [Nhu A.N., Son S., Lin M.C.]
  year: 2025
  venue: "ICML 2025 (arXiv:2506.08441)"
  category: direct-competitor
  role: "TAWM — explicitly conditions world model on time-step size Δt and trains over diverse Δt values for multi-rate dynamics learning. Built on TD-MPC2 (online MPC). KEY DISTINCTION from our work: (1) TAWM treats Δt conditioning as beneficial for performance/data-efficiency; we diagnose it as pathological in imagination-based actor-critic training (CIVO). (2) TAWM uses MPC (no imagination rollouts for policy training); our failure mode is specific to imagination-based training where the critic exploits dt-conditioned value estimates. (3) TAWM focuses on observation-rate robustness; we focus on value overestimation from temporal conditioning corruption. TAWM actually strengthens our contribution: it shows Δt conditioning works in MPC settings, making our finding that it fails in imagination-based settings a surprising and important diagnostic."
  relevance_score: 5
  novelty_threat: "MEDIUM — methodological overlap (Δt conditioning) but fundamentally different paradigm (MPC vs imagination) and opposite conclusion (beneficial vs pathological). Must cite and differentiate in paper."

- paper_id: li2025lsimagine
  title: "Open-World Reinforcement Learning over Long Short-Term Imagination"
  authors: [Li J., Wang Q., Wang Y., Jin X., Li Y., Zeng W., Yang X.]
  year: 2025
  venue: "ICLR 2025 Oral (arXiv:2410.03618)"
  category: direct-competitor
  role: "LS-Imagine — extends imagination horizon in Dreamer via goal-conditioned jumpy state transitions and affordance maps. Addresses the 'short-sightedness' of standard Dreamer imagination. KEY DISTINCTION: LS-Imagine adds jumpy transitions to reach long-horizon targets (open-world Minecraft), while our work shows that variable-dt imagination itself introduces CIVO. LS-Imagine's jumpy transitions use goal conditioning (not dt-embedding), potentially avoiding the value overestimation we identify."
  relevance_score: 4
  novelty_threat: "LOW — different mechanism (goal-conditioned jumps vs dt-embedding) and different focus (long-horizon exploration vs diagnostic of failure modes). Should cite as concurrent approach to extending imagination horizon."

- paper_id: zhang2026hwm
  title: "Hierarchical Planning with Latent World Models"
  authors: [Zhang W., Terver B., Zholus A., Chitnis S., Sutaria H., Assran M., Balestriero R., Bar A., Bardes A., LeCun Y., Ballas N.]
  year: 2026
  venue: "arXiv:2604.03208"
  category: direct-competitor
  role: "HWM — learns multi-scale latent world models for hierarchical MPC planning; high-level planner optimizes macro-actions, low-level planner handles primitives. 70% success on real-world non-greedy robotic tasks vs 0% for single-level. Addresses temporal abstraction via hierarchical planning (MPC), not imagination-based actor-critic. Further evidence that temporal abstraction in world models requires hierarchy rather than single-scale variable-dt approaches."
  relevance_score: 4
  novelty_threat: "LOW — MPC-based hierarchical planning, not imagination-based training. Supports our thesis that flat dt-embedding approaches are inferior to hierarchical alternatives."

- paper_id: kobayashi2025metacontroller
  title: "Emergent temporal abstractions in autoregressive models enable hierarchical reinforcement learning"
  authors: [Kobayashi S., et al.]
  year: 2025
  venue: "arXiv:2512.20605"
  category: method-component
  role: "MetaController — discovers temporal abstractions via higher-order non-causal sequence model controlling base autoregressive model's residual stream. Each controller executes behaviorally meaningful action sequences with learned termination conditions. Operates in fundamentally different paradigm (LLM-style autoregressive models, not world-model imagination), but demonstrates that temporal abstraction benefits from hierarchical structure rather than flat dt-conditioning."
  relevance_score: 3

- paper_id: shaj2023mts3
  title: "Multi Time Scale World Models"
  authors: [Shaj V., Gholam Zadeh S., Demir O., Douat L.R., Neumann G.]
  year: 2023
  venue: "NeurIPS 2023 (arXiv:2310.18534)"
  category: method-component
  role: "MTS3 — probabilistic multi-time-scale state space model with fast and slow latent dynamics for variable-rate prediction. Provides efficient inference across temporal scales. Foundational multi-rate dynamics architecture; our work shows that even with proper multi-rate modeling, the downstream actor-critic training in imagination can exploit temporal conditioning for value overestimation — a failure mode MTS3 does not address (it focuses on prediction quality, not policy training)."
  relevance_score: 4

- paper_id: splates2025
  title: "Stable Planning with Temporally Extended Skills"
  authors: [SPlaTES authors]
  year: 2025
  venue: "Reinforcement Learning Journal (RLC 2025)"
  category: method-component
  role: "SPlaTES — hierarchical MPC with temporally extended skills + abstract skill world model. Skill learning via mutual-information objective yields diverse, predictable, task-related behavior. Demonstrates that stable long-horizon planning requires modeling skill outcomes (temporal abstraction via hierarchy), not primitive-action outcomes at variable time steps — consistent with our finding that flat dt-embedding fails."
  relevance_score: 3

- paper_id: beckerehmck2023multitimestep
  title: "Multi-timestep models for Model-based Reinforcement Learning"
  authors: [Becker-Ehmck P., Peters J., van der Smagt P.]
  year: 2023
  venue: "arXiv:2310.05672"
  category: background
  role: "Proposes multi-timestep training objective (weighted sum of losses at various future horizons) for one-step dynamics models to improve long-horizon R² score. Addresses compounding error at the model training level; our work shows that even with perfect multi-step prediction, the imagination-based actor-critic can still fail due to value overestimation from dt-conditioning — a downstream failure mode distinct from prediction accuracy."
  relevance_score: 3

- paper_id: liu2022dmve
  title: "Dynamic-Horizon Model-Based Value Estimation With Latent Imagination"
  authors: [Liu Y., et al.]
  year: 2022
  venue: "IEEE TNNLS (arXiv:2009.09593)"
  category: background
  role: "DMVE — adaptive rollout horizon selection via horizon reliability detection (comparing value expansion errors between raw and reconstructed observations). Addresses the horizon selection problem in imagination-based value estimation. Complementary to our work: DMVE selects among fixed-dt horizons; we show that even optimal horizon selection cannot fix the CIVO when dt-embedding is trained (the overestimation is in the value function, not the horizon length)."
  relevance_score: 3

- paper_id: palenicek2025diminishing
  title: "Diminishing Return of Value Expansion Methods"
  authors: [Palenicek D., Lutter M., Carvalho J., Dennert D., Ahmad F., Peters J.]
  year: 2025
  venue: "Reinforcement Learning Journal (RLC 2025, arXiv:2412.20537)"
  category: evaluation
  role: "Shows longer model-based rollout horizons have diminishing returns in sample efficiency — even with oracle dynamics models, each additional expansion step yields progressively smaller gains. The bottleneck is NOT model accuracy. Directly supports our finding: extending imagination horizon via dt>1 does not improve performance because the problem lies in value estimation (CIVO from dt_embedding), not dynamics quality. Strengthens our argument that dt=1 imagination is sufficient."
  relevance_score: 5

- paper_id: kim2025deas
  title: "DEAS: DEtached value learning with Action Sequence for Scalable Offline RL"
  authors: [Kim C., Seo Y., et al.]
  year: 2025
  venue: "arXiv:2510.07730"
  category: method-component
  role: "Shows action sequences (temporal extension via options/semi-MDP) cause excessive value overestimation in actor-critic algorithms; proposes detached value learning where critic trains separately from policy. Parallel to our finding: temporal extension (whether via action sequences or dt-embedding) creates value overestimation in actor-critic; DEAS's detached learning is analogous to our dt=1 imagination fix (decoupling temporal abstraction from value estimation)."
  relevance_score: 4

- paper_id: luo2025vpl
  title: "A Case for Validation Buffer in Pessimistic Actor-Critic"
  authors: [Nauman M., Ostaszewski M., Cygan M.]
  year: 2025
  venue: "IJCAI 2025 (arXiv:2403.01014)"
  category: method-component
  role: "Validation Pessimism Learning (VPL) — uses validation buffer to adaptively adjust pessimism levels throughout training; shows pessimism is beneficial only during overestimation, detrimental during underestimation. Relevant to our setting: our trained dt_embedding creates persistent overestimation (nve>1.5x), suggesting adaptive pessimism could be a complementary mitigation to our dt=1 imagination restriction."
  relevance_score: 3

- paper_id: lenz2025macura
  title: "Trust the Model Where It Trusts Itself -- Model-Based Actor-Critic with Uncertainty-Aware Rollout Adaption"
  authors: [Lenz S., et al.]
  year: 2025
  venue: "arXiv:2405.19014"
  category: method-component
  role: "MACURA — uses model uncertainty to adaptively determine local rollout length in model-based actor-critic; avoids uniform rollout horizon. Addresses rollout quality from the uncertainty perspective; our work identifies a different mechanism: even if the model is confident, dt-embedding-conditioned imagination can produce overestimated value estimates (CIVO). MACURA's uncertainty-based termination would not catch our failure mode because the model predictions may be accurate while value estimates are corrupted."
  relevance_score: 3
